course_title: Multiliteracies and Numeracy Across Learning Areas

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate comprehensive and well-founded knowledge of the current nature of literacy and numeracy in the twenty first century
Critically review contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning across curricula
Apply contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning to teaching and learning design across learning areas
Design an action research project that investigates an aspect of multiliteracies and/or numeracy teaching and learning as a means of professional development and pedagogical improvement.

assessments.assessment_title: Action Research Problem statement, Literature Review and Inquiry Questions
assessments.task_description:
Reflecting on the benefits of action research for professional learning is a useful way of improving your understanding of your role as a practitioner and as an educational researcher. Across EDUC7113 the contemporary landscape of multiliteracies and numeracy will be mapped and explored. With this understanding you will identify a key multiliteracy or numeracy challenge or issue that you will explore across the semester. This will be the focus of Assessment 1, 2 and 3. 

Assessment Task 1 is the beginning of your action research project proposal. It consists of identifying the inquiry/problem, conducting a literature review and creating research questions.

Assessment Task 1 has 3 parts, and will be up to 2000 words total (excluding references):

 Part 1 – Problem Statement (approx. 250 words)

Action research in education is a cyclical, reflective research practice that many experienced teachers engage in. It often involves choosing a topic, framing the research problem statement and formulating specific research question/s (guided by the literature review) (Efron & David, 2020).

In Part 1 you are to define your inquiry focus by briefly describing the educational context and the challenge or issue you wish to address as a problem statement. You will be required to share your research topic, problem statement and potential research question/s (on the Blackboard Discussion and during class in week 2 or 3) to receive feedback from the Lecturer and your peers.

 Part 2 – Literature Review (approx.1500 words)

  • Conduct a literature review of the challenge or issue you identified in Part 1. Gather information from peer-reviewed academic literature, policies, reports, etc. to situate your problem within education context/s
  • Consolidate all this information into a literature review demonstrating synthesis, critical analysis, evaluation and identification of any gaps in research.
  • Discuss how this literature shapes your understanding of the topic and how it helps you justify your inquiry.


Part 3 – Research Question(s) (approx. 250 words)

  • Identify your key research question/s you are going to investigate
  • Explain how it/they are informed by your literature review

 

References

  • Efron, E.E, & Ravid, R. (2020). Action Research in Education : A Practical Guide, Guilford Publications https://ebookcentral.proquest.com/lib/uql/detail.action?docID=5928892

assessments.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Presentation, Portfolio, Poster
assessments.task_description:
For this task you will communicate your plan for your action research project in a format you feel best communicates the proposal. This choice is open to oral, written, presentation. audio-visual product, or a combination of the above. You may submit up to 2000 words, a presentation of up to 12 mins, poster, or a multimodal product of an equivalent length.  

Your submission in any of the formats, should cover:

  • Introduction: Briefly describe the research context and your problem statement (from Task 1) and describe how your literature review informed your research questions
  • Methodology: Describe the actions you will undertake and justify them with the research literature
  • Data, Analysis and Discussion:
  • Describe the data you propose to collect and how you will analyse it (including teaching strategy or lesson plan, etc. you intend to implement for the research).
  • Explain how your findings will answer your research questions and how this may inform your future practice.
  • Create an implementation plan with timeline 
  • Conclusion and implications: Reflect on what you have learned through your action research proposal, what implications your project might raise and how it may influence your future practice

assessments.task_description:
Students are required to reflect on their action research project in a one-one-one online meeting with the lecturer. They will briefly describe their project and learnings. They will be required to answer (unseen) reflective questions from the lecturer about their project, as well as situate their project in relation to the current landscape of multiliteracies and/or numeracy research.

Requirements

Students must show the examiner the surroundings of the computer/room prior to beginning the discussion. Students are permitted one A4 page of notes on the desk in front of them to consult during the meeting.
